item.research_question: Can high-throughput electrochemical screening results obtained from thin-film material libraries be reliably transferred to particulate catalysts for high-entropy oxide systems?
item.processing_route: Combinatorial reactive sputter deposition on 100 mm Si/SiO2 wafers using a four-cathode system (Co, Cr, Fe, Mn50Ni50 targets) with Ar/O2 flow (80/40 sccm) at 0.4 Pa; deposition temperatures of 573, 773, and 973 K; target permutations used to disentangle correlated gradients. Aerosol-based synthesis for particles using metal nitrate precursors in ethanol, sprayed onto a deflector plate, dried in a 1073 K furnace, and annealed at 773 K in oxygen flow.
item.test_conditions: Thin films: Scanning droplet cell (SDC) in 0.05 M KOH, 3-electrode system, LSV 1–1.8 V vs RHE, 10 mV s–1 scan rate. Particles: Rotating disk electrode (RDE) in 1 M KOH, 1600 rpm, LSV measurements with iR-correction.
key_findings: The most active thin-film composition identified was (Cr24.6±1.4Mn15.7±2.0Fe16.9±1.8Co26.1±1.9Ni16.6±1.7)37.8±0.8O62.2±1.2.
This hit composition exhibited an overpotential of 0.36 V at a current density of 1 mA cm–2.
The lattice constants of the single-phase spinel films ranged from 0.826 to 0.851 nm depending on composition.
The synthesized particles showed a composition of (Cr23Mn19Fe18Co25Ni15)-Ox with a diameter ranging from 75 nm to 1 μm.
The difference in overpotential between the thin film and the particle catalyst at 1 mA cm–2 was only 8 mV (thin film: 1.594 V, particles: 1.586 V vs RHE).
No correlation was found between surface roughness (Ra values of 1.2–4.8 nm) and electrochemical activity.
The highest OER activity was observed for compositions with high Cr, Ni, and Mn content, medium Co content, and low Fe content.
item.mechanism: The authors argue that the observed activity trends are driven by compositional changes rather than microstructure or sheet resistance, as resistance maps and activity maps did not show the same trends. They state that since OER is a surface reaction, the kinetics at low overpotentials are governed by species adsorption, allowing for reliable comparison between thin films and particles despite different measurement geometries.
item.limitations: The authors note that gradients of elements deposited from opposing targets are reversed, and neighboring targets have correlated gradients, which complicates the analysis of individual element contributions without the permutation method. They also mention that the low electrical conductivity of most oxide films required the use of a Pt electrode layer for SDC measurements, and that the resistance of the thin film variant B was not measured directly due to the underlying electrode layer.
item.future_work: The authors propose that combining theory, simulation, and machine learning with high-throughput experimentation can enable the prediction and understanding of new high-entropy materials, as no theoretical model currently exists that can reliably predict the electrochemical activity of HEMs.
quotes: We demonstrate the successful transfer of results from thin-film material libraries to particles of Cantor alloy oxide (Co-Cr-Fe-Mn-Ni)3O4.

The similar OER activity of the most active thin-film composition and the derived catalyst particles validates the proposed approach of accelerated discovery of novel catalysts by screening of thin-film libraries.
The difference in the overpotentials is only 8 mV (thin film: 1.594 V, particles: 1.586 V vs RHE), demonstrating very similar electrocatalytic OER activity.
